items.statement: Available historical compiled evidence is Tier-2 development-grade, ~15.94 days, and cannot support promotion.
Outcome integrity lacks cost-adjusted net-R and has only 210 complete outcomes of 790 cache rows; historical stage2 variants max at 2 complete outcomes.
Current Production WATCH freshness is severely delayed while FUEL-RICH is materially fresher; optimization metrics can be contaminated by observation latency.

Current callers use distinct ScoreV2 strict/watch and Entry Decision readiness contracts; timing, structure, and execution semantics differ. Intentional specialization versus drift/double-counting remains unresolved and is not a reproduced defect.

differences: timing: ScoreV2 includes two_closed_candles and volume_acceleration; Entry Decision has separate timing helper and >=10 timing gate
structure: ScoreV2 maximum 35 with support_broken; Entry Decision maximum 20
execution: strict ScoreV2 and Entry Decision both require complete/approved microstructure, but spread policy differs (0.50 vs 0.30 documented)

items.statement: Current cumulative evidence acquisition is REST-heavy: ws_share=0.036067 with 507 ws hits and 13550 REST fallbacks.
Current Production signal_ledger_total and signal_outcomes_total metrics are zero at baseline capture; new natural forward evidence is not yet available from these counters.

items.problem: Entry Decision is the sole canonical user-facing decision; lifecycle and ScoreV2 outputs are inputs/context, not independent entry instructions.
items.solution: Keep ranking, lifecycle-v2 shadow, leverage, and legacy scores non-authoritative; compare them through explicit crosswalks only.

items.problem: Observed WATCH evidence is delayed and acquisition is REST-heavy, so apparent model rejection/readiness differences are confounded by observation latency and availability.
items.solution: Repair/censor freshness and collect matched causal packets before comparing semantics or searching parameters.

items.problem: Available evidence cannot identify whether unresolved layer differences improve outcomes or merely alter availability.
items.solution: Collect immutable natural outcomes with cost-adjusted net-R and run preregistered matched replay/OOS evaluation.

items.problem: Leverage has independent causal/risk bounds and is not a readiness or lifecycle gate.
items.solution: Exclude leverage from model champion scoring; report unavailable/not-recommended without fallback.

items.problem: Measurement readiness is insufficient for scientific comparison or parameter search even though deterministic replay and layer-divergence measurements are possible.
items.solution: Run a preregistered matched crosswalk with causal freshness, explicit unavailable states, immutable outcome linkage, and cost-adjusted net-R before optimization.

items.problem: The current evidence pipeline does not yet provide a promotion-ready, point-in-time outcome denominator with complete costs and immutable cross-layer provenance.
items.solution: Implement and validate the staged data/outcome integrity controls in DATA_OUTCOME_INTEGRITY_PLAN.md before any parameter search.

items.problem: FP/FN attribution cannot be interpreted until stale/unavailable packets are separated from eligible outcomes and the three layer differences are compared on matched causal packets.
items.solution: Preregister and execute FP_FN_DIAGNOSIS_PROTOCOL.md only after measurement and outcome-integrity gates pass.

items.problem: Raw gate rejection counts cannot identify causal contribution because score, coverage, freshness, hard gates, trade-plan presence, and Anti-Chase may be mutually binding.
items.solution: Execute the paired single-gate and preregistered interaction ablations only after measurement and outcome-integrity gates pass.

items.problem: Existing persistence contains most causal decision fields, but complete realized cost fields and a normalized immutable signal-to-outcome export are not guaranteed.
items.solution: Build a research compiler/export from existing append-only records and reject or explicitly exclude incomplete cost/provenance rows.

items.problem: The stale WATCH population and low WS share are caused by an intentional WATCH acquisition policy plus backlog/throughput conditions; no scheduler/cache/WebSocket implementation defect was reproduced.
items.solution: Censor or repair stale WATCH observations and measure state-specific acquisition separately; do not patch or lower thresholds without a failing reproduction.
